# CALIBRATION REPORT

**Generated by:** `tests/calibration/run_calibration.py`
**Corpus:** 66 real PyTorch training runs, 200 steps each
**Wall time:** 95 s

## Corpus composition

| Fault class | Runs | Split | Expected detectors | Injection step |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `H0_healthy` | 6 (4+2) | cal 4 / hold 2 | (none) | — |
| `H1_heavy_tail_gradients` | 6 (4+2) | cal 4 / hold 2 | (none) | — |
| `H2_noisy_healthy_loss` | 6 (4+2) | cal 4 / hold 2 | (none) | — |
| `F1_isolated_loss_spike` | 6 (4+2) | cal 4 / hold 2 | loss.robust_zscore | 120 |
| `F2_sustained_divergence` | 6 (4+2) | cal 4 / hold 2 | loss.trend_slope, loss.robust_zscore | 120 |
| `F3_gradient_explosion` | 6 (4+2) | cal 4 / hold 2 | grad.robust_zscore | 120 |
| `F4_nan_loss` | 6 (4+2) | cal 4 / hold 2 | numerics.finiteness | 120 |
| `F5_inf_gradient` | 6 (4+2) | cal 4 / hold 2 | numerics.finiteness | 120 |
| `F6_throughput_degradation` | 6 (4+2) | cal 4 / hold 2 | throughput.regression | 120 |
| `F7_lr_discontinuity_no_failure` | 6 (4+2) | cal 4 / hold 2 | (none) | — |
| `F10_mixed_anomaly` | 6 (4+2) | cal 4 / hold 2 | grad.robust_zscore, loss.robust_zscore, numerics.finiteness | 120 |

Healthy-by-construction runs: **24**. Fault-injected runs: **42**.

`F7_lr_discontinuity_no_failure` and `H1_heavy_tail_gradients` are the
precision tests: both look like faults to a naive detector and are not.

**No threshold was tuned on either split.** The Phase 1 defaults were frozen
before this harness existed; the split exists so that a future tuning pass
cannot silently consume the holdout.

## Detector errors

None. Every detector ran to completion on every run.

## What these numbers do and do not support

* These are **detector-level** precision and recall on a synthetic fault corpus
  built from real training loops. They are not field precision on real incidents.
* The corpus is **66 runs**, of which 42 are fault-injected. The 95 % interval on
  a recall near 0.9 is roughly ±9 points at this sample size — wide. Per-class
  conclusions rest on only 6 runs each.
* Faults are injected at a **known single step** with a known mechanism. Real
  incidents arrive through data, hardware and configuration in ways this corpus
  does not model.
* `H1` and `F7` deliberately probe the boundary between healthy-looking and
  faulty; a detector that scores well on `F1`-`F6` and badly on `H1`/`F7` is
  overfitted to clean signals.
